Predictions: spe/predictions/r02.yaml (saved before the run)
Results: spe/evals/results/r02/r02.json (5 trials per cell, 40 tickets, 200 runs per cell)
Scoring: a pass rate counts as a hit if it is within 0.02 of the result. A cost counts as a hit if it is within 25%. Pass rate means category_acc.

Score: 3 of 6 hits.

Against the baseline: the mean absolute error on pass rate was 0.035 for my predictions and 0.030 for "same as last round". My predictions did worse than assuming nothing would change. The C miss alone caused this.

### Why claims

- B, "shorter prompt keeps focus": not supported. B tied A on category (0.86 and 0.86). B was 0.01 lower on priority (0.78 and 0.79). B did cut cost from $0.011 to $0.009 per ticket.
- C, "merged tools cut wrong tool choice": refuted. C made fewer tool calls (2.6 against 4.1 for A). C also skipped check_status on 9 outage tickets. See F4.
- D, "same design on a smaller model loses about 0.15": partly right. D lost 0.12 on category (0.74 against 0.86) and 0.13 on priority (0.66 against 0.79).

### Noise

One standard error near 0.85 with 200 runs is about 0.025. This is an estimate. It assumes independent runs, but the runs share the same 40 tickets, so the true error is larger. The 0.03 lead I predicted for B over A was inside the noise. I should not have written it as a gain. C sits 0.06 below A. That gap is about 1.6 standard errors of the difference. It is likely real but not certain. The F4 traces show a mechanism for it.

### Lessons for round 3

- For a change to the tool surface, predict the direction for each ticket class, such as outage tickets. Do not predict one overall number. I predicted C would improve without checking which steps the merge took out of the default path.
- Cost predictions must account for long inputs and retries. I priced D from token rates alone and missed F5.
- A predicted gain larger than one standard error needs a named mechanism I can check in a trace. Otherwise I predict "same as last round".
